exact_statement: For k >= 3, let F_k(n) be the minimum number of colours needed to colour an n-vertex graph with floor(n^2/4)+1 edges so that every C_(2k+1) is rainbow. For k=3, prove or refute that F_3(n) is asymptotic to n^2/8.
scope_notes: The inherited round-9 theorem concerns the exact two-independent-owner Boolean switch architecture G(m,r), not an arbitrary public hard branch.
This campaign first asks for an owner- and trace-preserving reduction from every relevant natural-switch state family to G(m,r).

If that is false, a valid outcome is the smallest exact switch-state counterbranch, with all of its states made C7-legal by a proved trace transversal and with the missing structural hypothesis named.
A synthetic switch-state counterbranch does not close the public problem unless it is additionally derived from every public hard branch or is itself a threshold hard graph.
No fixed-size census without a complete support reduction counts.
